correctness.rationale: Exact source RESULT.md proves conditional Wiener-growth E[W_(m+1)|T_m]=(1+2/m)W_m+m. Known mean a_m=m(m+1)H_m-2m² and root path mean m(H_m-1) give at marked arrival j the shift delta_j=3(j-1)-(j+1)H_(j-1). Independence of future uniform parents propagates this shift by product_{m=j}^{n-1}(m+2)/m=n(n+1)/(j(j+1)); multiply by P(I_j=1)=1/(j-1) to get displayed covariance. The g_j=(j+1)H_(j-1)/(j-1) increases for j>=3 via H_(j-1)<=j/2, with g_2=g_3=3. Summing finite harmonics gives the global expression and pi²/6 limiting coefficient. Independent enumeration of all 120 labeled recursive trees n=6 computed every Wiener distance and every local covariance exactly, agreeing. Zero covariance at j=2,3 is not independence.

value.rationale: Wiener index is a canonical global pairwise metric, and root child count a canonical local growth degree. The theorem resolves the arrival-wise sign profile (exact neutrality at j=2,3, strict negative thereafter for every final n) and gives an explicit nonzero quadratic scaling constant; the information is not recoverable from marginal Wiener or path-length means alone.

limitations: Uniform recursive-tree attachment, n>=j>=2; not preferential attachment.
Zero covariance does not imply independence; weak historical priority risk persists.
